newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - FX vols steady but firm on spot strength.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FX vols steady but firm on spot strength.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/mark and dollar/yen options were steady but firm just after noon on Friday as the U.S. dollar refused to be contained.
The dollar weakened against the German mark early in the session after the release of stronger than expected U.S. jobs data but roared back into positive territory by mid-morning.
U.S. jobs rose 262,000 in December compared with a forecast for 192,000, causing a selloff in the U.S. bond market which initially pressured dollar/mark.
However, as spot gained, dollar/mark volatilities spiked higher, reflecting the degree of concern in the market about the mark's downside potential, dealers said.
One OTC dealer said demand might represent a "convergence play" ahead of European Monetary Union. "It seems like the dollar's being considered an alternative," he said.
Another dealer said the movement in volatility was technically driven, as spot moved above 1.58 marks and 116 yen.
The first dealer agreed those levels played a role and noted an increasing demand for mark puts against the dollar.
"There's been quite a bit of demand and that's what's behind the increase in volatility. The demand for puts, or dollar calls, across the Europeans," he said.
He also noted increased corporate demand.
Finally, he said the early selloff in the U.S. dollar provided a buying opportunity in a market that remains very dollar-bullish.
"People are looking for any opportunity to get into the dollar," he said.
At 1215 CST/1815 GMT, implied volatility for one-month dollar/mark at-the-money options was 9.5/9.9 percent, up 0.10 percentage point from Thursday's U.S. close, dealers said.
Implied volatility for one-month dollar/yen options was steady at 8.7/9.0 percent.
A third dealer said he expects implied volatilities for both dollar/pairs to remain firm through next week.
"There's just too much stuff going on for people to get complacent now," he said, citing the choppy U.S. stock market, bond weakness and weakness in the Japanese stock market.

Implied volatility for one-month dollar/Canada options was holding firm at 4.65/4.95 percent, dealers said. The one-month 25 delta dollar/Canada risk reversal was trading 0.2/0.5 percent in favor of Canada calls.
Roughly $2.5 billion worth of six month 1.27 Canada calls and one-year 1.31 Canada calls was said to have gone through in the OTC options market this week, OTC dealers said.
